title: Three British Players Reach Wrexham Open Quarter-Finals
summary:
It was a great day for British tennis fans at the Lexus Wrexham Open in Wales, as three British players won their matches to reach the quarter-finals.

Alicia Dudeney led the way with a long, tough match. She beat Susan Bandecchi of Switzerland, the seventh seed, 6-3, 6-7, 6-4. The match lasted two hours and 51 minutes. A seed is a player ranked among the top hopefuls in a tournament. The win was Dudeney's seventh in a row. Next she will face Elsa Jacquemot of France.

Hannah Klugman, who is only 17, also played very well. She defeated Anna Siskova of the Czech Republic, who is ranked higher than her, 6-2, 6-4. Last year, Klugman reached the final of the French Open junior girls' tournament. She is now ranked 341st in the world and will play Rebecca Sramkova of Slovakia, the sixth seed.

Jodie Burrage made it three British players in the last eight by beating fourth seed Noma Noha Akugue 6-1, 7-6. The second set ended in a close tiebreak, 11-9. Burrage will next play Spain's Marina Bassols Ribera, the fifth seed.

There was also a big surprise. The top seed, Anna Blinkova, ranked 72nd in the world, lost 6-3, 6-2 to Suzan Lamens of the Netherlands.

The tournament runs from October 18 to 25 at the Wrexham Tennis and Padel Centre. Last year's champion, Mimi Xu from Swansea, chose to play in a tournament in Canada instead, so the strong play of the three British women has cheered home fans.

The quarter-finals are on Friday, the semi-finals on Saturday, and the final on Sunday.
why_it_matters: Smaller tournaments like Wrexham give young and rising players, such as 17-year-old Hannah Klugman, a stage to build experience and confidence.
